To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the level of the disparity between the price and value of a firm is negatively related to the cost of arbitrage, but the duration of the price-value disparity is positively related to the cost arbitrage.
the level of mispricing is negatively related to arbitrage costs and that the duration of mispricing is positively related to arbitrage cost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of arbitraging costs on the level of and duration of the divergence between price and accounting fundamentals.
the relationship between price and accounting-based value.
the impact of the costs of arbitrage on the level and the duration of the price-value relation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of arbitraging costs on the convergence of price and accounting based firm value is not necessarily negative.
, while arbitrageurs are able to reduce the level of disparity between price and fundamentals, arbitrage costs are likely to impede their ability to quickly and completely correct mispricing.
the effect of arbitrage costs is to reduce the disparity between price-to-value, but only in the short run.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of arbitrage costs affects the level of the disparity between the price and value, but the duration of this disparity may be affected by the potential rewards to arbitrageurs.
the level and duration effects of arbitrage costs are both theoretically and empirically important and must be considered when evaluating the impact of arbitraging activity on market efficiency.
we show that the level and duration are both affected by the costs of arbitrage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arbitrage costs may increase the amount of time it takes for the price to converge to its fundamental value.
arbitrageurs are risk-averse, so that the cost of arbitrage is not a simple function of transaction costs, but also of risk aversion.
arbitrageurs are not necessarily impeded from correcting mispricing by arbitrage costs.
